A Dell Pro Precision 5 16 (BIOS 0.4.53) running kernel 6.17.0-1011-oem emits this warning at boot: "WARNING: CPU: 6 PID: 55 at fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 kernfs_remove_by_name_ns+0xe9/0xf0 — kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory", raised from typec_unregister_partner -> ucsi_unregister_partner inside ucsi_handle_connector_change (workqueue events, Comm: kworker/6:0). Find the root cause in the kernel source and determine whether an existing fix is already present in this tree or upstream. typec_unregister_partner {"total_count":16,"incomplete_results":false,"items":[{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/torvalds/linux/commits/e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a","sha":"e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a","node_id":"MDY6Q29tbWl0MjMyNTI5ODplMGIyOTFmZTExNzk2NDAzN2UwYmEzODJlZmY0YmIzNjVkNTMxYzNh","html_url":"https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/torvalds/linux/commits/e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a/comments","commit":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/torvalds/linux/git/commits/e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a","author":{"date":"2026-06-11T15:12:01.000+08:00","name":"Chia-Lin Kao (AceLan)","email":"acelan.kao@canonical.com"},"committer":{"date":"2026-07-16T17:11:22.000+02:00","name":"Greg Kroah-Hartman","email":"gregkh@linuxfoundation.org"},"message":"usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind

connector_unbind() is the mirror of connector_bind(), but it is missing
the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:

    if (port_dev->child)
        typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);

When a Thunderbolt dock is unplugged, two teardown paths race:

1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets
   port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This
   leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at
   the USB device that is about to be freed.

2. usb_disconnect() then calls typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...),
   but port_dev->connector is already NULL, so the call is a no-op and
   port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

3. Concurrently, UCSI detects a PD partner-disconnect event and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling
   pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()
   -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting
   the typec/UCSI partner state.

This corruption leaves the Thunderbolt tunnel in an inconsistent state on
the next dock hot-plug.  On affected hardware the dock's I225/igc NIC fails
to enumerate: AER fires a slot reset while the igc driver is still
initialising ("PCIe link lost"), and the subsequent igc_reset attempt hits
igc_rd32 on an already-detached device:

    igc 0000:2e:00.0 eth0: PCIe link lost, device now detached

    __cfi_worker_thread+0x10/0x10

content.text:
usb: typec: ucsi: Fix race condition and ordering in port unregistration

A synchronization issue exists during port unregistration where pending
partner work items can race against workqueue destruction, leading to
use-after-free conditions:

  cros_ec_ucsi cros_ec_ucsi.3.auto: error -ETIMEDOUT: PPM init failed
  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000000
  RIP: 0010:__queue_work+0x83/0x4a0
  Call Trace:
    <IRQ>
    __cfi_delayed_work_timer_fn+0x10/0x10
    run_timer_softirq+0x3b6/0xbd0
    sched_clock_cpu+0xc/0x110
    irq_exit_rcu+0x18d/0x330
    fred_sysvec_apic_timer_interrupt+0x5e/0x80

Fix this by ensuring strict ordering and proper serialization during
teardown:

1. Move ucsi_unregister_partner() to the beginning of the teardown
sequence and protect it under the connector mutex lock.
2. Ensure all pending partner tasks are explicitly flushed and finished
before the workqueue is destroyed.
3. Switch from mod_delayed_work() to a cancel_delayed_work() and
queue_delayed_work() sequence. This guarantees that items currently marked
as pending won't be scheduled an additional time, preventing a double
release of resources which leads to the following crash:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
    0xdead000000000122: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  Workqueue: cros_ec_ucsi.3.auto-con2 ucsi_poll_worker
  RIP: 0010:ucsi_poll_worker+0x65/0x1e0
  Call Trace:
  <TASK>
    process_scheduled_works+0x218/0x6d0
    worker_thread+0x188/0x3f0
    __cfi_worker_thread+0x10/0x10
    kthread+0x226/0x2a0

To ensure these rules are applied identically across both the normal
teardown and the ucsi_init() error paths, consolidate the cleanup logic
into a new helper, ucsi_unregister_port().

Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Fixes: b9aa02ca39a4 ("usb: typec: ucsi: Add polling mechanism for partner tasks like alt mode checking")
Fixes: b13abcb7ddd8 ("usb: typec: ucsi: Fix NULL pointer access")
Fixes: fac4b8633fd6 ("usb: ucsi: Ensure connector delayed work items are flushed")
Signed-off-by: Andrei Kuchynski <akuchynski@chromium.org>
Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260707141736.1635698-1-akuchynski@chromium.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

## Conclusion

The warning is caused by a **teardown race between USB Type-C connector unbinding and UCSI partner removal**. The immediate offender is:

```text
drivers/usb/typec/class.c:typec_partner_unlink_device()
```

specifically its second `sysfs_remove_link()` call:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
```

When `dev` has already been unregistered, `dev->kobj.sd` is gone. `sysfs_remove_link()` passes that missing kernfs directory to `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`, which emits the warning and returns `-ENOENT`.

The relevant upstream fix exists, but **it is not in the checked-out tree**. The fix is:

```text
e0b291fe1179 usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
```

It was committed upstream on 2026-07-16, after this tree's `v7.0` snapshot (`028ef9c96`, 2026-04-12).

---

## Call chain

The observed UCSI workqueue path is present in the tree:

```text
ucsi_handle_connector_change()
  -> ucsi_unregister_partner()
     -> typec_unregister_partner()
        -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
           -> sysfs_remove_link()
              -> kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
```

### 1. UCSI receives the disconnect notification

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264`:

```c
static void ucsi_handle_connector_change(struct work_struct *work)
```

The work is serialized with the connector mutex at line 1275:

```c
mutex_lock(&con->lock);
```

For a connector-change event, the disconnect branch is at lines 1306–1325:

```c
if (change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE) {
	...
	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		...
	} else {
		ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
	}
}
```

### 2. UCSI unregisters the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138`:

```c
static void ucsi_unregister_partner(struct ucsi_connector *con)
```

After removing PD, cable, and alternate-mode state, it calls:

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1151`:

```c
typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
```

### 3. Type-C core unlinks USB devices from the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174`:

```c
void typec_unregister_partner(struct typec_partner *partner)
```

The function checks the cached USB-device pointers:

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1183–1191`:

```c
mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);

if (port->usb2_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
	port->usb2_dev = NULL;
}
if (port->usb3_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
	port->usb3_dev = NULL;
}
```

The offending helper is `typec_partner_unlink_device()` at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
					struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");

	if (partner->deattach)
		partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}
```

The `"typec"` link was originally created in the reverse direction by `typec_partner_link_device()` at lines 888–903:

```c
sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
```

Thus, the second removal at line 909 assumes that `dev->kobj` is still registered.

---

## Why kernfs reports “no directory”

The warning is not generated merely because the `"typec"` entry is absent.

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724–1734` shows the exact behavior:

```c
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, const char *name,
			     const struct ns_common *ns)
{
	...
	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n",
			name);
		return -ENOENT;
	}
```

Therefore:

```text
"no directory" == parent == NULL
```

For the failing call, the parent is the USB device's sysfs kobject:

```c
&dev->kobj
```

The likely sequence is:

1. `typec_partner_link_device()` creates the USB-device-side link named `"typec"` at `class.c:892`.
2. The USB device is subsequently unregistered during USB/component teardown.
3. Its sysfs/kernfs directory is removed, so its kobject no longer has a valid kernfs node.
4. UCSI concurrently processes the partner disconnect.
5. `typec_unregister_partner()` still sees `port->usb2_dev` or `port->usb3_dev`.
6. `typec_partner_unlink_device()` calls:

   ```c
   sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
   ```

7. `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` receives a null parent and warns at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731`.

The stale pointer is retained because the USB Type-C connector unbind path only clears the connector pointer:

`drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729`:

```c
static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector,
			     void *data)
{
	struct usb_port *port_dev = to_usb_port(dev);

	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
}
```

It does **not** call `typec_deattach()`. Consequently, the Type-C port's `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` fields are not cleared before the USB device disappears.

This matches the upstream commit description for `e0b291fe1179`: component unbind clears `port_dev->connector`, then USB disconnect can no longer perform the Type-C detach, leaving the Type-C port with a stale USB-device pointer. UCSI subsequently tries to remove the partner link through that stale device.

---

## Fixes already present in this tree

The checked-out tree is Linux `v7.0`, commit:

```text
028ef9c96e96197026887c0f092424679298aae8
```

It already contains the earlier fix:

```text
ec27386de23a usb: typec: class: Fix NULL pointer access
```

That fix added `partner_link_lock` and serialized:

- partner registration,
- partner unregistration,
- Type-C attach,
- Type-C detach.

The current tree contains the lock in `typec_unregister_partner()` at `class.c:1183`, and the lock is also used around partner registration and link operations.

That fix prevents concurrent Type-C core operations from racing with each other, but it cannot fix the separate lifetime problem where USB component unbind fails to detach the Type-C device at all.

The current tree still has the problematic unbind implementation at:

```text
drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729
```

with no `typec_deattach()` call.

---

## Upstream fix

The directly relevant upstream fix is:

```text
e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a
usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
```

Its essential change is to make `connector_unbind()` symmetric with `connector_bind()`:

- `connector_bind()` calls `typec_attach()` when a child USB device already exists.
- `connector_unbind()` must call `typec_deattach()` before clearing `port_dev->connector`.

That clears the Type-C port's cached USB-device pointer and removes the partner-side `"typec"` link while the USB device's sysfs directory is still valid.

### Related upstream series

There is also a separate, already-present Type-C locking fix:

```text
ec27386de23a usb: typec: class: Fix NULL pointer access
```

And a later UCSI teardown-order fix:

```text
7aa7d4bf9d3fa9a6a47b640ad103ab433b7ff261
usb: typec: ucsi: Fix race condition and ordering in port unregistration
```

The latter addresses pending UCSI partner work items racing with port/workqueue destruction. It is relevant to general UCSI teardown correctness, but it is not the direct cause of this particular kernfs `"typec", no directory` warning.

### Status summary

| Fix | Status in checked-out tree | Relevance |
|---|---:|---|
| `ec27386de23a` — Type-C partner-link locking | Present | Prevents concurrent Type-C link operations |
| `e0b291fe1179` — detach Type-C connector on component unbind | **Absent** | Direct fix for stale USB device pointer and this warning |
| `7aa7d4bf9d3` — UCSI port-unregistration ordering | Absent | Separate UCSI workqueue teardown race |

So, for the reported warning on the Dell system, the primary kernel defect is the missing `typec_deattach()` in `drivers/usb/core/port.c:connector_unbind()`, fixed upstream by `e0b291fe1179`.

|---|---:|---|

So, for the reported warning on the Dell system, the primary kernel defect is the missing `typec_deattach()` in `drivers/usb/core/port.c:connector_unbind()`, fixed upstream by `e0b291fe1179`.

## Conclusion

The warning is caused by a **teardown race between USB Type-C connector unbinding and UCSI partner removal**. The immediate offender is:

```text
drivers/usb/typec/class.c:typec_partner_unlink_device()
```

specifically its second `sysfs_remove_link()` call:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
```

When `dev` has already been unregistered, `dev->kobj.sd` is gone. `sysfs_remove_link()` passes that missing kernfs directory to `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`, which emits the warning and returns `-ENOENT`.

The relevant upstream fix exists, but **it is not in the checked-out tree**. The fix is:

```text
e0b291fe1179 usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
```

It was committed upstream on 2026-07-16, after this tree's `v7.0` snapshot (`028ef9c96`, 2026-04-12).

---

## Call chain

The observed UCSI workqueue path is present in the tree:

```text
ucsi_handle_connector_change()
  -> ucsi_unregister_partner()
     -> typec_unregister_partner()
        -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
           -> sysfs_remove_link()
              -> kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
```

### 1. UCSI receives the disconnect notification

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264`:

```c
static void ucsi_handle_connector_change(struct work_struct *work)
```

The work is serialized with the connector mutex at line 1275:

```c
mutex_lock(&con->lock);
```

For a connector-change event, the disconnect branch is at lines 1306–1325:

```c
if (change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE) {
	...
	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		...
	} else {
		ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
	}
}
```

### 2. UCSI unregisters the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138`:

```c
static void ucsi_unregister_partner(struct ucsi_connector *con)
```

After removing PD, cable, and alternate-mode state, it calls:

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1151`:

```c
typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
```

### 3. Type-C core unlinks USB devices from the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174`:

```c
void typec_unregister_partner(struct typec_partner *partner)
```

The function checks the cached USB-device pointers:

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1183–1191`:

```c
mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);

if (port->usb2_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
	port->usb2_dev = NULL;
}
if (port->usb3_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
	port->usb3_dev = NULL;
}
```

The offending helper is `typec_partner_unlink_device()` at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
					struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");

	if (partner->deattach)
		partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}
```

The `"typec"` link was originally created in the reverse direction by `typec_partner_link_device()` at lines 888–903:

```c
sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
```

Thus, the second removal at line 909 assumes that `dev->kobj` is still registered.

---

## Why kernfs reports “no directory”

The warning is not generated merely because the `"typec"` entry is absent.

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724–1734` shows the exact behavior:

```c
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, const char *name,
			     const struct ns_common *ns)
{
	...
	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n",
			name);
		return -ENOENT;
	}
```

Therefore:

```text
"no directory" == parent == NULL
```

For the failing call, the parent is the USB device's sysfs kobject:

```c
&dev->kobj
```

The likely sequence is:

1. `typec_partner_link_device()` creates the USB-device-side link named `"typec"` at `class.c:892`.
2. The USB device is subsequently unregistered during USB/component teardown.
3. Its sysfs/kernfs directory is removed, so its kobject no longer has a valid kernfs node.
4. UCSI concurrently processes the partner disconnect.
5. `typec_unregister_partner()` still sees `port->usb2_dev` or `port->usb3_dev`.
6. `typec_partner_unlink_device()` calls:

   ```c
   sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
   ```

7. `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` receives a null parent and warns at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731`.

The stale pointer is retained because the USB Type-C connector unbind path only clears the connector pointer:

`drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729`:

```c
static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector,
			     void *data)
{
	struct usb_port *port_dev = to_usb_port(dev);

	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
}
```

It does **not** call `typec_deattach()`. Consequently, the Type-C port's `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` fields are not cleared before the USB device disappears.

This matches the upstream commit description for `e0b291fe1179`: component unbind clears `port_dev->connector`, then USB disconnect can no longer perform the Type-C detach, leaving the Type-C port with a stale USB-device pointer. UCSI subsequently tries to remove the partner link through that stale device.

---

The directly relevant upstream fix is:

```text
e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a

```

Its essential change is to make `connector_unbind()` symmetric with `connector_bind()`:

- `connector_bind()` calls `typec_attach()` when a child USB device already exists.
- `connector_unbind()` must call `typec_deattach()` before clearing `port_dev->connector`.

That clears the Type-C port's cached USB-device pointer and removes the partner-side `"typec"` link while the USB device's sysfs directory is still valid.

A synchronization issue exists during port unregistration where pending
partner work items can race against workqueue destruction, leading to
use-after-free conditions:

  cros_ec_ucsi cros_ec_ucsi.3.auto: error -ETIMEDOUT: PPM init failed
  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000000
  RIP: 0010:__queue_work+0x83/0x4a0
  Call Trace:
    <IRQ>
    __cfi_delayed_work_timer_fn+0x10/0x10
    run_timer_softirq+0x3b6/0xbd0
    sched_clock_cpu+0xc/0x110
    irq_exit_rcu+0x18d/0x330
    fred_sysvec_apic_timer_interrupt+0x5e/0x80

Fix this by ensuring strict ordering and proper serialization during
teardown:

1. Move ucsi_unregister_partner() to the beginning of the teardown
sequence and protect it under the connector mutex lock.
2. Ensure all pending partner tasks are explicitly flushed and finished
before the workqueue is destroyed.
3. Switch from mod_delayed_work() to a cancel_delayed_work() and
queue_delayed_work() sequence. This guarantees that items currently marked
as pending won't be scheduled an additional time, preventing a double
release of resources which leads to the following crash:

    0xdead000000000122: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI

    worker_thread+0x188/0x3f0
    __cfi_worker_thread+0x10/0x10
    kthread+0x226/0x2a0

teardown and the ucsi_init() error paths, consolidate the cleanup logic
into a new helper, ucsi_unregister_port().

usb: typec: ucsi: Fix race condition and ordering in port unregistration

A synchronization issue exists during port unregistration where pending
partner work items can race against workqueue destruction, leading to
use-after-free conditions:

  cros_ec_ucsi cros_ec_ucsi.3.auto: error -ETIMEDOUT: PPM init failed
  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000000
  RIP: 0010:__queue_work+0x83/0x4a0
  Call Trace:
    <IRQ>
    __cfi_delayed_work_timer_fn+0x10/0x10
    run_timer_softirq+0x3b6/0xbd0
    sched_clock_cpu+0xc/0x110
    irq_exit_rcu+0x18d/0x330
    fred_sysvec_apic_timer_interrupt+0x5e/0x80

Fix this by ensuring strict ordering and proper serialization during
teardown:

1. Move ucsi_unregister_partner() to the beginning of the teardown
sequence and protect it under the connector mutex lock.
2. Ensure all pending partner tasks are explicitly flushed and finished
before the workqueue is destroyed.
3. Switch from mod_delayed_work() to a cancel_delayed_work() and
queue_delayed_work() sequence. This guarantees that items currently marked
as pending won't be scheduled an additional time, preventing a double
release of resources which leads to the following crash:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
    0xdead000000000122: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  Workqueue: cros_ec_ucsi.3.auto-con2 ucsi_poll_worker
  RIP: 0010:ucsi_poll_worker+0x65/0x1e0
  Call Trace:
  <TASK>
    process_scheduled_works+0x218/0x6d0
    worker_thread+0x188/0x3f0
    __cfi_worker_thread+0x10/0x10
    kthread+0x226/0x2a0

To ensure these rules are applied identically across both the normal
teardown and the ucsi_init() error paths, consolidate the cleanup logic
into a new helper, ucsi_unregister_port().

Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Fixes: b9aa02ca39a4 ("usb: typec: ucsi: Add polling mechanism for partner tasks like alt mode checking")
Fixes: b13abcb7ddd8 ("usb: typec: ucsi: Fix NULL pointer access")
Fixes: fac4b8633fd6 ("usb: ucsi: Ensure connector delayed work items are flushed")
Signed-off-by: Andrei Kuchynski <akuchynski@chromium.org>
Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260707141736.1635698-1-akuchynski@chromium.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

FILES

ec27386de23a 2025-04-11T12:57:36Z usb: typec: class: Fix NULL pointer access
e0b291fe1179 2026-07-16T15:11:22Z usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind

## Conclusion

The warning is caused by a **teardown race between USB Type-C connector unbinding and UCSI partner removal**. The immediate offender is:

```text
drivers/usb/typec/class.c:typec_partner_unlink_device()
```

specifically its second `sysfs_remove_link()` call:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
```

When `dev` has already been unregistered, `dev->kobj.sd` is gone. `sysfs_remove_link()` passes that missing kernfs directory to `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`, which emits the warning and returns `-ENOENT`.

The relevant upstream fix exists, but **it is not in the checked-out tree**. The fix is:

```text
e0b291fe1179 usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
```

It was committed upstream on 2026-07-16, after this tree's `v7.0` snapshot (`028ef9c96`, 2026-04-12).

---

## Call chain

The observed UCSI workqueue path is present in the tree:

```text
ucsi_handle_connector_change()
  -> ucsi_unregister_partner()
     -> typec_unregister_partner()
        -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
           -> sysfs_remove_link()
              -> kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
```

### 1. UCSI receives the disconnect notification

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264`:

```c
static void ucsi_handle_connector_change(struct work_struct *work)
```

The work is serialized with the connector mutex at line 1275:

```c
mutex_lock(&con->lock);
```

For a connector-change event, the disconnect branch is at lines 1306–1325:

```c
if (change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE) {
	...
	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		...
	} else {
		ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
	}
}
```

### 2. UCSI unregisters the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138`:

```c
static void ucsi_unregister_partner(struct ucsi_connector *con)
```

After removing PD, cable, and alternate-mode state, it calls:

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1151`:

```c
typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
```

### 3. Type-C core unlinks USB devices from the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174`:

```c
void typec_unregister_partner(struct typec_partner *partner)
```

The function checks the cached USB-device pointers:

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1183–1191`:

```c
mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);

if (port->usb2_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
	port->usb2_dev = NULL;
}
if (port->usb3_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
	port->usb3_dev = NULL;
}
```

The offending helper is `typec_partner_unlink_device()` at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
					struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");

	if (partner->deattach)
		partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}
```

The `"typec"` link was originally created in the reverse direction by `typec_partner_link_device()` at lines 888–903:

```c
sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
```

Thus, the second removal at line 909 assumes that `dev->kobj` is still registered.

---

## Why kernfs reports “no directory”

The warning is not generated merely because the `"typec"` entry is absent.

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724–1734` shows the exact behavior:

```c
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, const char *name,
			     const struct ns_common *ns)
{
	...
	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n",
			name);
		return -ENOENT;
	}
```

Therefore:

```text
"no directory" == parent == NULL
```

For the failing call, the parent is the USB device's sysfs kobject:

```c
&dev->kobj
```

The likely sequence is:

1. `typec_partner_link_device()` creates the USB-device-side link named `"typec"` at `class.c:892`.
2. The USB device is subsequently unregistered during USB/component teardown.
3. Its sysfs/kernfs directory is removed, so its kobject no longer has a valid kernfs node.
4. UCSI concurrently processes the partner disconnect.
5. `typec_unregister_partner()` still sees `port->usb2_dev` or `port->usb3_dev`.
6. `typec_partner_unlink_device()` calls:

   ```c
   sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
   ```

7. `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` receives a null parent and warns at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731`.

The stale pointer is retained because the USB Type-C connector unbind path only clears the connector pointer:

`drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729`:

```c
static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector,
			     void *data)
{
	struct usb_port *port_dev = to_usb_port(dev);

	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
}
```

It does **not** call `typec_deattach()`. Consequently, the Type-C port's `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` fields are not cleared before the USB device disappears.

This matches the upstream commit description for `e0b291fe1179`: component unbind clears `port_dev->connector`, then USB disconnect can no longer perform the Type-C detach, leaving the Type-C port with a stale USB-device pointer. UCSI subsequently tries to remove the partner link through that stale device.

---

## Fixes already present in this tree

The checked-out tree is Linux `v7.0`, commit:

```text
028ef9c96e96197026887c0f092424679298aae8
```

It already contains the earlier fix:

```text
ec27386de23a usb: typec: class: Fix NULL pointer access
```

That fix added `partner_link_lock` and serialized:

- partner registration,
- partner unregistration,
- Type-C attach,
- Type-C detach.

The current tree contains the lock in `typec_unregister_partner()` at `class.c:1183`, and the lock is also used around partner registration and link operations.

That fix prevents concurrent Type-C core operations from racing with each other, but it cannot fix the separate lifetime problem where USB component unbind fails to detach the Type-C device at all.

The current tree still has the problematic unbind implementation at:

```text
drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729
```

with no `typec_deattach()` call.

---

## Upstream fix

The directly relevant upstream fix is:

```text
e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a
usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
```

Its essential change is to make `connector_unbind()` symmetric with `connector_bind()`:

- `connector_bind()` calls `typec_attach()` when a child USB device already exists.
- `connector_unbind()` must call `typec_deattach()` before clearing `port_dev->connector`.

That clears the Type-C port's cached USB-device pointer and removes the partner-side `"typec"` link while the USB device's sysfs directory is still valid.

### Related upstream series

There is also a separate, already-present Type-C locking fix:

```text
ec27386de23a usb: typec: class: Fix NULL pointer access
```

And a later UCSI teardown-order fix:

```text
7aa7d4bf9d3fa9a6a47b640ad103ab433b7ff261
usb: typec: ucsi: Fix race condition and ordering in port unregistration
```

The latter addresses pending UCSI partner work items racing with port/workqueue destruction. It is relevant to general UCSI teardown correctness, but it is not the direct cause of this particular kernfs `"typec", no directory` warning.

### Status summary

| Fix | Status in checked-out tree | Relevance |
|---|---:|---|
| `ec27386de23a` — Type-C partner-link locking | Present | Prevents concurrent Type-C link operations |
| `e0b291fe1179` — detach Type-C connector on component unbind | **Absent** | Direct fix for stale USB device pointer and this warning |
| `7aa7d4bf9d3` — UCSI port-unregistration ordering | Absent | Separate UCSI workqueue teardown race |

So, for the reported warning on the Dell system, the primary kernel defect is the missing `typec_deattach()` in `drivers/usb/core/port.c:connector_unbind()`, fixed upstream by `e0b291fe1179`.
